summary.intent: Fix a failing Linux CI job on PR #537 by diagnosing why the move-content E2E test's verifier was reporting all files as undecryptable.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified as a test-infra bug from PR #532: the verifier was spawning `node node_modules/.bin/tsx` (a shell shim, not JS), causing a SyntaxError. Fixed by switching to `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs` and pushed to #537.

repo: node_modules/.bin/tsx is a shell shim (#!/bin/sh), not a JS file — invoking it via `node` causes a SyntaxError; use `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs` instead
The move-content test's verify() spawns a child tsx process, unlike other E2E tests that use `pnpm exec tsx` (shell-executed shim)
The #532 migration introduced this broken spawn pattern in test-move-content.ts

code.finding: verify() was spawning `node node_modules/.bin/tsx <script>` — fixed to use `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs` via a TSX_CLI constant

workflow: When a verifier reports consistent failure across all N attempts, suspect the verifier's own launch mechanism before assuming product or infra bugs
Cross-platform tsx invocation via node requires pointing at the real JS entry point (dist/cli.mjs), not the shell shim in .bin/

friction: The real error (SyntaxError on shell shim) was hidden behind a misleading symptom ('file not decryptable' on all 24 attempts), requiring dedicated diagnostic tooling to surface
The bug was introduced in a prior PR (#532) and only manifested on Linux CI, not locally
open_items: Audit other desktop E2E .mjs/test scripts for the same broken `node .bin/tsx` spawn pattern introduced in #532 — this file was fixed but others may have the same issue
